chunks: He said: "We have put your people on trial in your absence; and Sameri has led them astray."

key_terms.السَّامِرِيُّ: Sameri (a specific individual, often identified as a man from the tribe of Benjamin or a craftsman, who made the calf)
key_terms.فَتَنَّا: We tested/tried (implying a trial or temptation)

ai.seo_question: Who was Sameri and how did he lead the Israelites astray during Musa's absence?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, As-Samiri is often viewed not merely as an individual but as a symbol of the tendency toward materialism and deviation during the Prophet's or Imam's absence (Ghaybah). This verse highlights the specific trial faced by Bani Israel, where the golden calf incident served as a test of faith and a precursor to the broader theme of divine guidance versus human error. The mention of 'fitnah' (trial/tribulation) underscores the spiritual vulnerability of the community when left without direct leadership.
